transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Ethan Moore (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Jimenez (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Larkspur Head of Data), Marisol Vega (Larkspur CISO), Owen Walsh (Larkspur Platform Eng), Tara Lee (Larkspur Compliance)

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick agenda — run through your constraints, evidence needs, and then talk hosting modes and next steps.
[00:12] Daniel: Yeah, thanks. We want to map out whether Redwood Hosted is feasible or if we need Dedicated or fully Private. Primary concerns are audit evidence for financial regulators, plus some HIPAA overlap — we process some health claims for investment-backed healthcare benefits.
[00:30] Marisol: And from security perspective, we need control over KMS keys, strong tenant isolation, and guaranteed log residency. Can't have raw transcripts leaving the country for certain clients.
[00:45] Priya: Understood. Quick clarifying q: when you say "log residency" — do you mean the raw request/response payloads and the platform audit logs?
[00:52] Marisol: both. We need application request logs for troubleshooting but they need to be redacted and held in-region. Audit logs that show who invoked what must be exportable to our SIEM.
[01:03] Owen: Also, legal hold — we have retention and e-discovery rules. If there's a legal hold request we might need to freeze certain tenant artifacts. How does Redwood handle legal holds?
[01:12] Carlos: On Dedicated/Private we can arrange retention and export hooks; Hosted has retention defaults but we do offer export and longer retention via enterprise settings. Legal hold is possible but we need to scope it with our legal ops.
[01:25] Daniel: What about KMS? Our policy is keys must either be customer-managed and remain in-eu for EU clients, or be HSM-backed with explicit escrow controls.
[01:35] Priya: For Private deployment we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM directly. For Dedicated we support BYOK with our cloud KMS in a dedicated keyspace, and we have HSM options — there are some vendor integration caveats. For Hosted, BYOK is limited to certain regions and providers.
[01:50] Tara: Any certification evidence available for the deployment? We need SOC2 type 2, ISO 27001, and pen test reports for procurement.
[02:00] Ethan: We have SOC2, ISO 27001 and a summarized pen test report. I'll share the complete evidence pack after this call. Also, we can provide mapping worksheets to show how our controls map to your regulator's checklist.
[02:11] Marisol: Can you explain how logs are partitioned? We can't have cross-tenant logs accessible by other customers or by engineers without RBAC.
[02:20] Carlos: Logs are tenant-scoped; on Dedicated and Private we can guarantee physical isolation for log storage. On Hosted, logs are logically separated and encrypted per-tenant, and we maintain strict RBAC. But for auditors you usually prefer dedicated storage locations.
[02:40] Daniel: Transcription question — our concern is that raw model outputs might contain customer PII. Does Redwood store model responses in KV cache or logs?
[02:50] Priya: We have options. Persistent KV cache can be configured to avoid storing full responses; caching can be disabled for sensitive routes. We also offer automatic redaction for defined fields (PII masks) before logs are written. That redaction engine is configurable and we can run sample payloads to test.
[03:10] Owen: Latency implications? We operate in low-latency trading windows for some clients, can't add more than ~10ms per request overhead. How does Dedicated compare to Hosted?
[03:20] Carlos: Dedicated has more predictable p99 latency because you get reserved GPUs and no noisy neighbors. Hosted is optimized but has multi-tenant factors; we can present benchmarks. For extreme low-latency we suggest a Dedicated pool colocated in your primary region.
[03:40] Marisol: For EU-only data, we need both keys and logs kept in eu-west-1. Is region-locking available?
[03:48] Priya: Region-locking is part of Private or Dedicated with a region-only tenancy. Hosted has region selection but not full region-lock enforcement for backups and control-plane metadata in some cases. We'll include the exact control-plane residency notes in the evidence pack.
[04:05] Daniel: If we go Dedicated, what's the typical onboarding timeline and what steps require our infra team?
[04:12] Ethan: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 4-8 weeks: contract, infra provisioning, KMS/HSM integration, networking (VPC peering or private link), and testing. If you want Private/on-prem it's longer and we do a partner-assisted deployment.
[04:30] Tara: On e-discovery, can you export raw logs in a format our legal team can use? We may need CSV or parquet with provenance metadata.
[04:38] Carlos: Yes, export endpoints are available; for Private and Dedicated we can stream logs to your S3 with encryption and object-level ACLs. We can also support export formats and include provenance headers.
[05:00] Daniel: A question on audit: regulators ask for chain-of-custody on logs — who handled changes, timestamps, integrity checks?
[05:10] Priya: Our audit pipeline includes immutable append-only logs with checksums. For Dedicated/Private we can provide a signed digest and a rotation history. We'll document the chain-of-custody process.
[05:25] Marisol: Anything about model provenance? If we need to demonstrate which model/version produced an output, how do you capture model metadata?
[05:33] Carlos: Every request includes model id/version, kernel/quantization profile, and a generation metadata blob. We keep that with the trace. For Hosted that's stored per request too; for Dedicated you can choose retention policy.
[05:50] Ethan: Ok, sounds like we're lining up. Next immediate items: we'll share SOC2 pack, KMS integration guide, and a short worksheet for sample payload redaction. Carlos will run a short benchmark plan.
[06:05] Daniel: Good. Quick procurement note — we prefer having legal review the MSA before pilot. So pricing ballpark and MSA draft would be helpful.
[06:15] Ethan: I'll send a draft MSA and a pricing estimate for a modest Dedicated pool.

[06:30] --- (conversation continues with technical clarifications, noise/crosstalk) ---

[22:10] Priya: (walkthrough) if you look at the HSM import, there are two flows: import a wrapping key into our KMS or use a proxy to sign requests. The import flow requires temporary key export which some banks won't allow, so we support integration with certain HSM vendors over a key-escrow model.
[22:35] Marisol: We can't do key export, so we'd be interested in the proxy signing model or a Private on-prem install.
[23:00] Carlos: Noted. We'll prepare a vendor compatibility matrix.

[30:12] Owen: For logging we have an existing SIEM on-prem. Can we ship audit events with assured delivery and signatures?
[30:22] Carlos: Yes, we have a secure delivery pipeline with retries and signed events; integration via Kafka or S3 is supported.

[38:05] Tara: One edge case — do you keep transient debug dumps that may contain sensitive tokens? We need assurance those are ephemeral and access-controlled.
[38:14] Priya: Debug dumps are gated; for Dedicated we can disable debug dumps entirely or route them to a customer-controlled bucket.

[45:40] Daniel: Anything else from Redwood?
[45:46] Ethan: We'll follow up with the evidence packet, propose demo slots, and share the MSA and dedicated pricing. Also will include redaction sample and HSM vendor list.
[45:59] Marisol: We'll compile the list of regulated data fields and forward.
[46:07] Ethan: Great. Thanks all.

[52:00] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript has minor speaker id errors typical of meeting auto-transcribe; multiple pauses and clarifications omitted for brevity.
